principles: Prove every remaining group with fresh deterministic machine checks, not prose-only status updates.
Keep local baseline evidence clearly separated from Authority, production, fullAuthority, and remote-host claims.
Make the aggregate command fail closed unless all 150 rows and the documented group matrix are represented.
Change evaluator core only where the documented baseline cannot honestly be represented by task-level smokes alone.
drivers: The user asked to finish all remaining groups, not just update the document.
The baseline exists specifically to prevent false DONE on large multi-milestone work.
G05 deferral semantics must prevent deferred work from becoming full roadmap DONE.

options.name: A: implement G04-G10 group smokes plus aggregate smoke with one narrow evaluator correction
pros: Produces independent commands and aggregate proof.
Fixes the discovered G05 semantic mismatch rather than hiding it.
cons: Larger story than one group at a time.
Requires careful review to avoid changing unrelated lifecycle behavior.

options.name: B: implement only G04 next and leave G05-G10 future
cons: Does not satisfy the user request to complete the remaining groups.
Would prolong the very partial-DONE risk the baseline is meant to catch.

options.name: C: implement smokes only and encode G05 as invalid deferral without core change
cons: Would not match the documented G05 expected matrix.
Would turn valid deferral into an invalid-row scenario and weaken the proof.

chosen: A: implement G04-G10 group smokes plus aggregate smoke with one narrow evaluator correction
rationale: Choose option A because it is the only path that completes all remaining baseline groups, preserves aggregate proof, and honestly fixes the discovered G05 deferral semantics gap.

preMortem.scenario: The story claims the full 10x15 baseline is complete before every group command passes.
preMortem.trigger: Documentation is updated ahead of executable evidence or aggregate proof.
preMortem.consequence: The baseline itself becomes a false-DONE example.
preMortem.mitigation: Each checklist item requires a group command PASS, and CHK-008 requires the aggregate 150-row command PASS before docs claim full implementation.

preMortem.scenario: The evaluator correction for G05 changes unrelated closure semantics.
preMortem.trigger: A broad refactor changes closed row handling for evidence-backed or not-applicable rows.
preMortem.mitigation: Limit edits to deferred-row rollup semantics and run parent-roadmap-totality-smoke plus all large-ledger group smokes.

preMortem.scenario: Local synthetic baseline proof is overclaimed as Authority or production completion.
preMortem.trigger: G07 or docs use elevated terms without explicit negative-boundary wording.
preMortem.consequence: Users mistake local deterministic smokes for external runtime certification.
preMortem.mitigation: Run overclaim guard assertions and docs grep; final summary must state no Authority, fullAuthority, production, or remote-host claim.

preMortem.scenario: Aggregate smoke counts command PASS strings instead of evaluating all 150 rows.
preMortem.trigger: The aggregate command shells out to group smokes but does not verify row totals and matrix semantics.
preMortem.consequence: A missing group or malformed row could hide behind PASS text.
preMortem.mitigation: Aggregate command must compute and assert the 10x15 group matrix, including total evaluated row count 150.
